questions.question: An administrator is upgrading a Zurich instance to the Brazil release. What happens to the ITSM Enhanced Security Features plugin (com.snc.itsm.enhanced_security) during the upgrade?

options.text: It is activated automatically and adds deny-unless-authenticated ACLs
It stays inactive until it is requested from ServiceNow Support
It is activated on new instances, but upgrades leave it inactive
It is removed, and its ACL rules are merged into the existing itil role

explanation.correct: The Brazil upgrade information says the ITSM Enhanced Security Features plugin is now activated automatically when you upgrade to Brazil. Before this, it was activated only on new instances. Activating it adds "deny unless authenticated" ACL rules to several IT Service Management tables. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-changemanagement-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Support is involved only if you want to go back to the old behavior: "To revert to the pre-upgrade behavior, contact ServiceNow Support for a list of ACLs to deactivate on specific tables." The plugin itself is activated automatically.
This was the behavior before the change ("Previously, the plugin was activated only on new instances"). Now the plugin is also activated automatically on upgrade.
The release notes say that activating the plugin adds new ACL rules. They do not say it is removed or merged into the itil role.

documentation.section: Change Management - Important information for upgrading

source.excerpt: The ITSM Enhanced Security Features plugin ( com.snc.itsm.enhanced_security ) is now activated automatically when you upgrade to the Brazil release.

questions.question: After upgrading to Brazil, a change process owner is given the granular sn_change_admin role introduced in the Australia release, so they can configure Change Management features and system properties. Which three roles does sn_change_admin include? (Choose three.)

options.text: sn_change_writer
change_manager
sn_change_cab.cab_manager
sn_incident_admin
sn_trigger_table_cfg_write

explanation.correct: The Australia "Granular admin role" note says the sn_change_admin role grants permission to configure Change Management features and system properties, and that it includes the sn_change_writer, change_manager, and sn_change_cab.cab_manager roles. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-changemanagement-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: sn_incident_admin is the Australia granular admin role for Incident Management ("Configure all Incident Management features including incident management properties"). It is not part of sn_change_admin.

sn_trigger_table_cfg_write is one of the roles contained in the Australia On-Call Scheduling granular role sn_on_call_admin ("It contains sn_trigger_table_cfg_read and sn_trigger_table_cfg_write roles"). It is not part of sn_change_admin.

source.excerpt: The sn_change_admin role includes the sn_change_writer, change_manager, and sn_change_cab.cab_manager roles.

questions.question: On a Brazil instance, a change manager starts a change lockdown for a critical financial event. A normal change is already scheduled inside the lockdown period. What does conflict detection do with that change request?

options.text: It flags it as an Inside Change Lockdown conflict and puts it on hold
It cancels the change request and notifies the change's assignment group
It converts it to an emergency change that can bypass the lockdown
It sends it to the CAB for override approval while work continues

explanation.correct: Brazil change lockdown conflict detection automatically flags change requests that overlap an active lockdown period: "Any change request inside a lockdown is marked as an Inside Change Lockdown conflict and placed on hold." Rescheduling it outside the lockdown clears the conflict. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-changemanagement-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The change is not cancelled. It is placed on hold, and you "Reschedule it outside the lockdown period to clear the conflict and continue processing."
The release notes do not describe any conversion to an emergency change. The documented way to clear the conflict is to reschedule outside the lockdown period.
The change does not keep progressing. It is placed on hold until it is rescheduled outside the lockdown period. The release notes do not mention a CAB override.

source.excerpt: Any change request inside a lockdown is marked as an Inside Change Lockdown conflict and placed on hold.

questions.question: A compliance team at a bank on the Brazil release must record whether each change handles personal data and how long a rollback takes, without changing the Change Request table schema. How does Compliance dynamic schema store these details?

options.text: As name and value pairs saved in a single field on the change
As new columns added to the Change Request table per attribute
As child records in a related table, one record per attribute
As structured journal entries in the change request work notes

explanation.correct: Compliance dynamic schema (Brazil) stores risk and compliance details "without adding columns to the Change Request table" and "saves these details as name and value pairs in a single field using the platform Dynamic Schema feature." See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-changemanagement-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The feature exists to avoid this: it stores the details "without adding columns to the Change Request table."
The values are not stored as separate related records. They are saved "as name and value pairs in a single field" on the change request.
Work notes are not used. The values are kept in a single dynamic schema field, and scripts can read and update them through the dynamic schema scripting API.

source.excerpt: Compliance dynamic schema saves these details as name and value pairs in a single field using the platform Dynamic Schema feature.

questions.question: On a newly provisioned Brazil (zboot) instance, an agent has put an incident On Hold with the reason Awaiting Caller Information. The caller ignores every reminder notification. What happens once all attempts are used up?

options.text: It is resolved with the code Resolved - No response from caller
It is cancelled automatically, and the caller gets a notification
It returns to In Progress and is reassigned to the group manager
It stays On Hold until an agent resolves the incident manually

explanation.correct: The Brazil "Auto resolve On-hold incident" feature (zboot instances) sends the caller reminders for a set number of attempts. "If the caller does not respond after all attempts are exhausted, the incident is automatically resolved with the resolution code Resolved - No response from caller." By default there are 3 attempts, 1 business day apart. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-incidentmanagement-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The incident is resolved, not cancelled. The release notes give the resolution code Resolved - No response from caller and a resolution note saying the caller did not respond.
The incident goes back to In Progress only if the caller responds (comments on the Service Portal or replies to the email). Then the assigned agent is notified, not the group manager.
No manual step is needed. The incident is resolved automatically once all attempts are used up.

source.excerpt: If the caller does not respond after all attempts are exhausted, the incident is automatically resolved with the resolution code Resolved - No response from caller.

questions.question: A security administrator on a newly provisioned Brazil (zboot) instance is checking what the incident manager [incident_manager] role contains. Which role replaced the inherited itil role in incident_manager?

options.text: incident_write
sn_incident_admin
sn_mim_admin
sn_tcm_admin

explanation.correct: The Brazil "Incident manager role changes" note says: "The inherited itil role is now removed from the incident manager [incident_manager] role and replaced with the incident_write role." This applies only to zboot instances and limits access to incident records. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-incidentmanagement-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: sn_incident_admin is the Australia granular admin role used to configure Incident Management features and properties. It is not what replaced itil in incident_manager.
sn_mim_admin is the Australia granular admin role for configuring Major Incident Management features and trigger rules.
sn_tcm_admin is the Australia granular admin role for configuring Task Communications Management features.

source.excerpt: The inherited itil role is now removed from the incident manager [incident_manager] role and replaced with the incident_write role.

questions.question: A service desk manager on a Brazil instance has set the glide.ui.autoclose.time property to 5. When are resolved incidents now closed automatically?

options.text: Five business days after the incident is resolved
Five calendar days after the incident is resolved
Five hours after the incident is resolved
After five reminder notifications to the caller

explanation.correct: The Brazil "Auto close resolved incidents behavior changes" note says: "The resolved incidents are now automatically closed after a specific number of business days instead of calendar days." The number is set in glide.ui.autoclose.time, and 0 turns the feature off. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-incidentmanagement-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Calendar days was the earlier behavior. Brazil counts business days "instead of calendar days."
The property is described as the "Number of days (integer) after which Resolved incidents are automatically closed". It is a number of days, not hours.
Counting reminders to the caller is part of the On Hold auto-resolve feature (Awaiting Caller Information). The auto-close property counts business days after resolution.

source.excerpt: The resolved incidents are now automatically closed after a specific number of business days instead of calendar days.

questions.question: After upgrading from Zurich to Brazil, an administrator wants to give a team lead the granular role introduced in Australia for configuring all on-call schedule features, including properties and trigger rules. Which role should they assign?

options.text: On-call administrator [sn_on_call_admin]
Shift administrator [rota_admin]
Shift manager [rota_manager]
Premium Dashboard user [rota_prem_dashboard_user]

explanation.correct: The Australia "Granular role for on-call schedule configurations" note says: "Configure on-call schedule features using the granular and specific role, sn_on_call_admin." The On-Call Scheduling roles page says a user with sn_on_call_admin "can configure all on-call schedule features including its properties and trigger rules", and that the role contains rota_admin. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-oncallscheduling-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: rota_admin is the shift administrator role. It can create, read, update, and delete shifts and can modify shifts and rosters, but it is contained in sn_on_call_admin rather than being the granular configuration role introduced in Australia.
rota_manager is for the manager of a group. It lets a member manage shifts for that group, and "The role cannot be used to manage all groups on the instance."
rota_prem_dashboard_user only gives "Access to the On-Call Premium dashboard", which shows performance metrics across groups.

source.excerpt: Configure on-call schedule features using the granular and specific role, sn_on_call_admin. It contains sn_trigger_table_cfg_read and sn_trigger_table_cfg_write roles.

questions.question: An administrator is planning the Brazil upgrade and had set com.snc.on_call_rotation.log_escalations to false on the Zurich instance. What do the Brazil release notes say about this property?

options.text: It defaults to true, and the existing value is kept after upgrade
It defaults to true, and the upgrade resets the value to true
It defaults to false, and the upgrade resets the value to false
It is removed, and every on-call escalation is now logged automatically

explanation.correct: The Brazil "Escalation logging is true by default" note says the com.snc.on_call_rotation.log_escalations property, which controls whether on-call escalations are logged, "is enabled by default. After upgrade, the existing value on this property remains unaffacted" [sic]. So the false value set on Zurich is kept. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-oncallscheduling-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The default is true, but the upgrade does not change an existing value: "After upgrade, the existing value on this property remains unaffacted."
The property is enabled (true) by default in Brazil, and the upgrade keeps the existing value.
The property still exists. The escalation log page says you can enable or disable logging with com.snc.on_call_rotation.log_escalations.

source.excerpt: Escalation logging is true by default.

questions.question: A catalog manager on a Brazil instance finds that users subscribed to a parent service offering can open a catalog item even though they fail its "Available for" user criteria. What should the administrator do to block them?

options.text: Set glide.sc.catalog_item.subscription_enforcement to require_criteria
Keep glide.sc.catalog_item.subscription_enforcement at its default, allow_bypass
Add these users to the Secondary owner field on the catalog item
Activate the com.glideapp.servicecatalog.ui16_portal plugin

explanation.correct: Brazil adds the glide.sc.catalog_item.subscription_enforcement property. The require_criteria mode "Prevents access to users who don't meet the item's criteria, even if they are subscribed to the parent service offering." See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-servicecatalog-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: allow_bypass is the default and keeps the existing behavior, so subscribed users would still get access. That is the problem the administrator wants to fix.
The Secondary owner field (Australia) lets other users edit catalog items. It does not control who can request them.
This plugin moves requesters from the Core UI catalog experience to the Angular portal. It does not enforce user criteria.

source.excerpt: require_criteria: Prevents access to users who don't meet the item's criteria, even if they are subscribed to the parent service offering.

questions.question: After upgrading to Brazil, a user whose only role is catalog_admin can no longer open Requested Item [sc_req_item] records through the catalog-owned ACLs. What change in Brazil explains this?

options.text: Catalog roles were removed from the request management ACL records
The request management ACL records on sc_req_item were deleted
The ACL records now require the admin role as well as catalog_admin
The catalog_admin role was deprecated and removed from the instance

explanation.correct: The Brazil Service Catalog deprecation "Removal of Catalog Roles from request management ACLs" says ACL records on request management tables such as sc_request and sc_req_item "no longer grant access based on the catalog role or the catalog admin role." Users with only a catalog-related role and no request management role can no longer use these ACLs. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-servicecatalog-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The ACL records were not deleted. "Each ACL record retains at least one request management role, so the list is never empty."
The ACL records now keep only request management roles in their required roles. The release notes do not add the admin role.
The role was not removed. The change "affects only the ACL records that the catalog team owns", and catalog roles no longer appear in them.

source.excerpt: ACL records on request management tables and fields no longer grant access based on the catalog role or the catalog admin role.

questions.question: An administrator on a Brazil instance that was upgraded from Zurich wants requesters to see the Angular portal instead of the Core UI catalog when they request items. What must they do?

options.text: Install the com.glideapp.servicecatalog.ui16_portal plugin
Nothing, because the portal plugin is active by default after upgrade
Set glide.sc.catalog_item.subscription_enforcement to allow_bypass
Install the Universal Request plugin (com.snc.universal_request)

explanation.correct: The Brazil "Migration from Core UI to Angular portal" note says: "Administrators on upgraded instances must install the com.glideapp.servicecatalog.ui16_portal plugin to move from the Core UI catalog experience to the Angular portal." See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-servicecatalog-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The plugin is active by default only on new instances ("On new instances, the plugin is active by default"). Upgraded instances must install it.
This property controls whether service subscriptions can bypass "Available for" user criteria. It does not change the catalog experience.
com.snc.universal_request activates Universal Request, which is a separate product. It does not switch the catalog to the Angular portal.

source.excerpt: Administrators on upgraded instances must install the com.glideapp.servicecatalog.ui16_portal plugin to move from the Core UI catalog experience to the Angular portal.

questions.question: An administrator on an instance upgraded to Australia wants UI16 module links, such as forms and lists, to redirect to the equivalent Service Operations Workspace experience. Which system property must be set to true?

options.text: sn_sow_itsm_admin.experience_redirection_enabled.sow
glide.knowman.recent_task.display
change.conflict.useprogressworker
sn_change_cab.com.snc.change_management.cab.use_sow_meeting

explanation.correct: The Australia "UI16 links to SOW redirection behavior" note says redirection is supported for all applications in SOW "when the system property sn_sow_itsm_admin.experience_redirection_enabled.sow is set to true." New instances have it in the base system, and on upgraded instances administrators configure it from SOW Admin Center. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-serviceoperationsworkspaceforitsm-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: glide.knowman.recent_task.display (Zurich) shows the recent task records that a knowledge article was attached to. It does not redirect UI16 links.
change.conflict.useprogressworker chooses between Flow and Progress Workers for change conflict detection.
This property controls how CAB meetings are opened from the CAB Meeting workbench. It does not control UI16 link redirection.

documentation.section: Service Operations Workspace for ITSM - New features

source.excerpt: The UI16 module link redirection behavior is supported for all the applications in SOW when the system property sn_sow_itsm_admin.experience_redirection_enabled.sow is set to true.

questions.question: A service desk agent on a Brazil instance has attached a knowledge article to an incident in Service Operations Workspace. Where does the Attached knowledge related list appear by default?

options.text: On the Related records tab of the incident
On the Overview tab of the incident
In the contextual side panel of the incident
On the Details tab of the incident

explanation.correct: The Brazil "Default Attached knowledge related list" change says: "The attached knowledge related list now appears in the Related records tab by default, if any Knowledge article attached to the incident record." See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-serviceoperationsworkspaceforitsm-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Overview tab holds items such as the Summary section and the AI summary and suggestions card. The release notes put the Attached knowledge list on the Related records tab.
In these release notes, the contextual side panel is where DEX actions from the Action library run. The Attached knowledge list goes on the Related records tab.
The Details tab is where the AI summary card appears when Overview is hidden. The Attached knowledge list goes on the Related records tab by default.

documentation.section: Service Operations Workspace for ITSM - Changes

source.excerpt: The attached knowledge related list now appears in the Related records tab by default, if any Knowledge article attached to the incident record.

questions.question: An IT communications lead on an Australia instance wants to check how the Employee Slate for ITSM home page card shows service health during an incident. How are the items displayed?

options.text: Active outages first with a red accent, then maintenance in amber
Scheduled maintenance first in red, then active outages in amber
Active outages first in amber, then scheduled maintenance in red
Outages and maintenance shown in one combined list, sorted by start date

explanation.correct: The Australia "Viewing outages and maintenance" note for Employee Slate for ITSM says: "Active outages appear first with a red accent, followed by scheduled maintenance with an amber accent." When nothing is active, the card says "All systems operational". See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-employeeslateforitsm-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This reverses the order and colors. Active outages come first, in red.
This swaps the colors. Outages use a red accent and scheduled maintenance uses amber.
The card does not combine them into one list by date. Active outages are shown first, followed by scheduled maintenance, each with its own accent color.

documentation.section: Employee Slate for ITSM - New features

source.excerpt: Active outages appear first with a red accent, followed by scheduled maintenance with an amber accent.

questions.question: An administrator on an Australia instance wants to try the Universal Request Router agentic workflow, which helps employees get support that spans multiple departments. Which plugin makes Universal Request available?

options.text: com.snc.universal_request
com.glideapp.servicecatalog.ui16_portal
com.snc.on_call_rotation
com.snc.itsm.enhanced_security

explanation.correct: The Australia activation information says: "Universal Request is available with activation of the Universal Request plugin (com.snc.universal_request)." In Australia, the Universal Request Router agentic workflow helps employees with services that need support from multiple departments. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-universalrequest-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This plugin moves upgraded instances from the Core UI catalog experience to the Angular portal. It does not activate Universal Request.
This is the On-Call Scheduling plugin, which is active by default for zBoot customers. It is not Universal Request.
This is the ITSM Enhanced Security Features plugin. It adds "deny unless authenticated" ACL rules to ITSM tables.

source.excerpt: Universal Request is available with activation of the Universal Request plugin (com.snc.universal_request).

questions.question: A customer using Simplified IT Service Management on Australia wants to delegate setup work without granting admin. Which roles does Simplified ITSM use to configure Incident Management and Request Management?

options.text: sn_incident_admin for incidents and sn_request_admin for requests
itil for incidents and catalog_admin for requests
sn_incident_write for incidents and sn_request_write for requests
sn_mim_admin for incidents and sn_tcm_admin for requests

explanation.correct: The Australia Simplified IT Service Management notes say: "Configure Incident Management using the sn_incident_admin role and Request Management using the sn_request_admin role." See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-simplifieditservicemanagement-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: itil and the catalog roles are not the documented configuration roles. In Brazil, request management ACLs also "no longer grant access based on the catalog role or the catalog admin role."
sn_incident_write and sn_request_write are granular write roles from the ITSM Roles plugin, which other roles inherit for record access. Configuration uses sn_incident_admin and sn_request_admin.
sn_mim_admin configures Major Incident Management, and sn_tcm_admin configures Task Communications Management. Neither is used to configure Incident or Request Management.

documentation.section: Simplified IT Service Management - New features

source.excerpt: Configure Incident Management using the sn_incident_admin role and Request Management using the sn_request_admin role.

questions.question: A service desk agent (fulfiller) on a Brazil instance needs to escalate an incident through an AI client connected to the ITSM MCP Server, but sn_itsm_mcp_server.requester.escalate is turned off by default. Which tool should they use?

options.text: sn_itsm_mcp_server.incident.modify with escalate and escalation_reason
sn_itsm_mcp_server.request.modify with an urgency and escalation reason
sn_itsm_mcp_server.incident.get_details with the escalate input
task_approval_decision with a reject decision on the incident

explanation.correct: The deprecation note says: "The sn_itsm_mcp_server.requester.escalate tool is turned off by default. Use sn_itsm_mcp_server.incident.modify with the escalate and escalation_reason inputs instead." The tool changes also say a fulfiller can use incident.modify to escalate incidents. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-itsmmcpserver-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: sn_itsm_mcp_server.request.modify is the renamed requester.add_comment tool. Requesters use it to add customer-visible comments to requested items, not to escalate incidents.
sn_itsm_mcp_server.incident.get_details reads incident fields and lets a requester check an incident's status. It does not escalate.
task_approval_decision approves or rejects your oldest pending approval for a change or requested item. It does not escalate incidents.

source.excerpt: Use sn_itsm_mcp_server.incident.modify with the escalate and escalation_reason inputs instead.

questions.question: An administrator on a Brazil instance is getting ready to connect an external AI client to the ITSM MCP Server. Which three plugins must be activated? (Choose three.)

options.text: Now Assist for ITSM (sn_itsm_gen_ai)
Model Context Protocol Server (sn_mcp_server)
ITSM MCP Server (sn_itsm_mcp_server)
ITSM Roles (com.snc.itsm.roles)
ITSM Virtual Agent Lite (com.snc.itsm.virtualagent.lite)

explanation.correct: The ITSM MCP Server activation information lists the plugins to activate to use ITSM MCP Server: Now Assist for ITSM plugin (sn_itsm_gen_ai), Model Context Protocol Server (sn_mcp_server), and ITSM MCP Server (sn_itsm_mcp_server). Users also need the sn_mcp_server.viewer role as the base role. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-itsmmcpserver-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The ITSM Roles plugin provides granular roles such as sn_incident_write. It is not in the list of plugins required for the ITSM MCP Server.
ITSM Virtual Agent Conversation Topics Lite is being prepared for future deprecation in Brazil, and it is not a prerequisite for the ITSM MCP Server.

source.excerpt: Activate these plugins to use ITSM MCP Server: Now Assist for ITSM plugin (sn_itsm_gen_ai) Model Context Protocol Server (sn_mcp_server) ITSM MCP Server (sn_itsm_mcp_server)

questions.question: An ITSM platform owner is reading the Brazil release notes for ServiceNow Otto for ITSM to plan a chatbot roadmap. Which plugin is being prepared for future deprecation?

options.text: ITSM Virtual Agent Lite (com.snc.itsm.virtualagent.lite)
Learning Enhanced Automation Platform (sn_itom_leap)
ITSM Enhanced Security Features (com.snc.itsm.enhanced_security)
Model Context Protocol Server (sn_mcp_server)

explanation.correct: The Brazil deprecations for ServiceNow Otto for ITSM say: "ITSM Virtual Agent Conversation Topics Lite ( com.snc.itsm.virtualagent.lite ) is being prepared for future deprecation." ITSM Virtual Agent pre-built topics are also being prepared for future deprecation. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-servicenowottoforitservicemanagementitsm-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: LEAP is the replacement, not the item being deprecated. The Suggested steps skill "is being replaced with Learning Enhanced Automation Platform (LEAP)", and you install the sn_itom_leap plugin to move to it.
This plugin is activated automatically when you upgrade to Brazil. It is not being deprecated.
sn_mcp_server is one of the plugins you must activate to use the ITSM MCP Server in Brazil. It is not being deprecated.

documentation.section: ServiceNow Otto for IT Service Management (ITSM) - Deprecations

source.excerpt: ITSM Virtual Agent Conversation Topics Lite ( com.snc.itsm.virtualagent.lite ) is being prepared for future deprecation.
